## The question {#question}

::: {.nhh}
::: {.box .have}
What do we have?

- a **closed surface mesh** of the volume $V$ (liver)
- $N = 4n \approx 400\,000$ terminal nodes, **4 colours** (trees A, P, V, B),
  $n \approx 100\,000$ per colour
- now: every terminal gets the **same share** of the volume
:::

::: {.arrow}
→
:::

::: {.box .how}
What is asked?

Split $V$ into cells so that every cell

1. contains **at least one point of each colour**
2. is **one connected region inside** $V$
3. is **compact**, roughly round (Voronoi-like)

and return the **volume of every cell**.
:::

::: {.arrow}
→
:::

::: {.box .need}
What for?

- one cell = one sinusoid compartment that **couples all four trees**
- compartment volume from the **real geometry** instead of an equal split
:::
:::

## Why is it hard? {#difficulties}

::: {.cards}
::: {.card}
**$V$ is not a box**

- the first specification used Delaunay + **mirror points** across the faces of a box
- exact only for **convex** volumes with flat faces
- in a non-convex $V$ (e.g. a U-shape), Voronoi neighbours can touch **only outside** $V$
  → "connected in the graph" ≠ "connected in space"
:::

::: {.card}
**No package in Julia**

- what is needed: a 3D Voronoi diagram **restricted to a mesh** (restricted Voronoi diagram)
- Julia: Voronoi in **2D** only, Delaunay in 3D — no restricted 3D Voronoi
- exists in **C++** (Geogram) → would need a C wrapper, its own build and maintenance
:::

::: {.card}
**Colours and size**

- every cell must have **all 4 colours** — a constraint across groups of points,
  not only distances
- every cell must stay **connected** while points are moved between cells
- $N \approx 400\,000$ points, $\approx 11$ million voxels → must run in about a minute
:::
:::

## Three options {#options}

::: {.cards}
::: {.card .c-a}
**A · Mirror points**

Delaunay of the points + their mirror images across the faces of $V$

- exact volumes
- **only for convex polyhedra** ✗
:::

::: {.card .c-b}
**B · Voxels** ✓ chosen

Fill $V$ with small cubes, give each cube to its nearest point

- pure Julia, **any shape**
- connections never pass through the outside
- volumes ≈ 1 % per final cell (estimate)
:::

::: {.card .c-c}
**C · Restricted Voronoi (Geogram, C++)**

Exact cells of every point, cut to $V$

- exact volumes
- C++ library, wrapper **never compiled**
- kept as a fallback if exact volumes are needed
:::
:::

::: {.small .center .muted}
Central idea of B: every point owns the part of $V$ closest to it (its **small cell**).
A final cell is a **group of points** → after the voxel step, everything is done on a graph.
:::

## Pipeline {#pipeline}

::: {.pipeline-tbl}
| Step | What | Result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 0 · 1a | voxel size, inside test, nearest point per voxel | `owner` |
| 1c · 1b · 1d · 1e | one piece per small cell, volumes, neighbour graph, points without voxels | graph |
| 2 · 3 | seeds, grow cells on the graph | `label` |
| 4 · 5 · 6 | find cells missing a colour, repair, smooth | all cells colourful |
| 7 · 8 · 9 | label map, cell volumes, checks | cells + volumes |
:::

::: {.small .center .muted}
The graph ignores colours — neighbours are defined only by touching in space.
Colours enter only in steps 4–6.
:::

## Steps 0 · 1a — grid, inside test, owners {#s0-1a}

:::: {.columns .step-figs}
::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step1_0_grid.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[0]{.tag} **Voxel grid**

- mean spacing $s = (\mathrm{vol}(V)/N)^{1/3}$
- voxel size $h = s/3$ → ≈ 27 voxels per point
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step1_1a_inside.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[1a]{.tag} **Inside test**

- per column: where does it **cross the surface**?
- crossings alternate enter / leave
- odd number → hole in the mesh, column skipped
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step1_1a_owners.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[1a]{.tag} **Owners**

- every inside voxel → its **nearest point** (KD-tree)
- the voxels of a point = its **small cell**
:::
:::
::::

## Steps 1c · 1b — one piece per small cell, volumes {#s1c-1b}

:::: {.columns .step-figs}
::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step1_1c_before.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[1c]{.tag} **Before**

- near thin parts, a point can own voxels on **both sides of a gap**
- its small cell has **two pieces**
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step1_1c_after.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[1c]{.tag} **After**

- each point keeps its **home piece**
- a stray piece goes to the neighbour it shares the **most faces** with
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step1_1b_volumes.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[1b]{.tag} **Small-cell volumes** (after 1c)

- voxels owned × $h^3$
- sum ≈ $\mathrm{vol}(V)$
:::
:::
::::

## Steps 1d · 1e — the neighbour graph {#s1d-1e}

:::: {.columns .step-figs}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](figures/partition/step1_1d_graph.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[1d]{.tag} **Neighbour graph**

- two points are **neighbours** if their voxels **share a face**
- outside voxels belong to nobody → **no edge through the outside**
- colours are ignored
:::
:::

::: {.column width="20%"}
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}
![](figures/partition/step1_1e_orphan.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[1e]{.tag} **Points without voxels**

- a very close neighbour wins all their voxels
- one edge to the **nearest point that has voxels**; its colour still counts
:::
:::
::::

## Step 2 — seeds {#s2}

:::: {.columns .step-figs}
::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step2a_random_seeds.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[2]{.tag} **Random seeds**

- $m \approx n/4$ random data points
- ≈ 16 points, ≈ 4 of each colour per cell
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step2b_lloyd.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[2]{.tag} **Lloyd rounds**

- 3–5 rounds: points → nearest seed, seed → **mean** of its points
- even spacing → cells of **similar size**
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step2c_snap.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[2]{.tag} **Snap**

- every seed → its **nearest data point**, duplicates dropped
- a mean can fall outside $V$
:::
:::
::::

## Steps 3 · 4 — grow cells, count colours {#s3-4}

:::: {.columns .step-figs}
::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step3a_growing.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[3]{.tag} **Growing**

- multi-source **Dijkstra** on the graph
- edge length $\lVert p_i - p_j \rVert$
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step3b_grown.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[3]{.tag} **Grown**

- every point takes the label of the seed closest **along the graph**
- every cell is **connected** and compact
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step4_counts.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[4]{.tag} **Count colours**

- points of each colour per cell
- a cell missing a colour is **deficient** (≈ 2 % per colour expected)
:::
:::
::::

## Steps 5 · 6 — repair and smoothing {#s5-6}

:::: {.columns .step-figs}
::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step5a_path.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[5]{.tag} **Path to the missing colour**

- search outward from the deficient cell for the **nearest point of the missing colour**
- accepted only if every cell losing points keeps **all colours** and stays **connected**
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step5b_repaired.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[5]{.tag} **Repaired**

- the path joins the cell
- no acceptable path after ~20 tries → **merge** with a neighbouring cell
:::
:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
![](figures/partition/step6_smoothing.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[6]{.tag} **Smoothing (optional)**

- a boundary point moves to the cell with the **closer centre**
- only if both cells stay valid
:::
:::
::::

## Steps 7 · 8 · 9 — result and checks {#s7-9}

:::: {.columns .step-figs}
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](figures/partition/step7_label_map.pdf){width="100%"}

::: {.steps}
[7]{.tag} **Label map**

- every voxel gets the cell of its owner
- 3D: an image of the cells (VTK)
:::
:::

::: {.column width="5%"}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.steps}
[8]{.tag} **Cell volumes**

- sum of the small-cell volumes of the cell's points

[9]{.tag} **Checks**

- every cell has **all colours**
- every cell is **one piece** in space (flood fill over its voxels)
- $\sum$ cell volumes $= (\text{inside voxels}) \cdot h^3 \approx \mathrm{vol}(V)$
- accuracy: rerun with $h/1.5$, compare cell volumes
:::
:::
::::

## Status and next steps {#status}

::: {.text-06}
- **everything is a plan**; the first steps (0 – 1e) are being written in
  `src/trees_processing/terminal_nodes/colorful_partition/` with tests on a box mesh
- expected cost for $N = 400\,000$: about **a minute**, memory < 1 GB
  (start Julia with `-t auto`)

**Next**

1. run steps 0 – 1e on the real mesh and terminal nodes
2. write steps 2 – 9
3. validate on a box (compare with the mirror-point method) and on an L-shaped volume
4. connect the cells to the terminal part $T$ of the simulation
:::
